newsitem.title: USA: U.S. blue chips, led by techs, extend rebound.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blue chips, led by techs, extend rebound.

text.p: U.S. blue chips posted their third-consecutive winning session on Tuesday, lifted by resurgent high-technology stocks.
After a late-session rally the Dow industrials closed up 53 points, or 0.8 percent, to 6609.

With the rise, the closely watched 30-stock average has recovered 132 points in the past three sessions. In the recent sell-off, the Dow gave back 608 points between its record closing high of 7085 on March 11 and its closing last Thursday at 6477.
"I think folks are looking at prices, thinking they're reasonably attractive, and stepping up a little bit," said Robert von Pentz, a managing partner at Columbia Partners.
There was no runaway rally on Tuesday, however, with advancing issues issues edging decliners by a narrow 13-to-11 ratio on the New York Stock Exchange.

Technology shares, which had sold off in advance of the broader market, have led the recent advance. The tech-heavy Nasdaq composite on Tuesday rose six points, or about 0.5 percent, to 1257, its fourth straight gain.

Traders and analysts said technology stocks, particularly semiconductor makers, got a boost from stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings from Motorola Inc and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. They also cited positive comments on the group from Goldman Sachs strategist Abby Joseph Cohen.
Motorola ended off 1-5/8 at 59-1/2 after rising in advance of its earnings report. Advanced Micro rose 3/8 to 43-3/8.
Among other technology issues, Texas Instruments Inc rose 3-1/2 to 88-7/8, Microsoft Corp added 2-3/8 to 98-1/4 and Dell Computer Corp gained five to 78-3/4.
The rise in stocks came despite a weak Treasury market, where the 30-year bond was off 12/32 to yield in late trading, its yield rising to 7.10 percent from Monday's close at 7.07 percent.

While trading in the past weeks has been dominated by concern over rising interest rates, first-quarter earnings reports will take over as the focus on Wall Street in the coming sessions, analysts said.
"From now on it looks like it's going to depend on earnings," said Harry Laubscher, market analyst at Tucker Anthony.
Bank stocks, also featured by Goldman's Cohen, rallied. Citicorp rose 2-3/4 to 114-3/4, J.P. Morgan & Co Inc gained 2-1/8 to 101-3/8 and Chase Manhattan Corp added 2-5/8 to 96-7/8.
Viking Office Products Inc sank 5-1/2 to 14-1/2 after forecasting that results for its third quarter ended March 31 would fall short of Wall Street estimates.
Shares of Transocean Offshore Inc gained 2-3/4 to 61-5/8. The company said it had received letters of intent to contract two of its deepwater drilling rigs.
JLG Industries Inc, a maker of aerial work platforms, tumbled 5-5/8 to 13-3/4 after it said its quarterly earnings may fall short of analysts' expectations.
The S&P 500 index rose 3.99 points to 766.12.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 6.02 points to 1257.37.
